questions: Where exactly is the sharp “knife-stroke” pain located (e.g., throat, chest, head/behind the eyes, ear, sinus area, or abdomen)?
Do you have trouble swallowing saliva or difficulty breathing (any choking, drooling, or noisy breathing)?
Do you have trouble opening your mouth fully or any “muffled/hot potato” voice with drooling?
answers: It’s in my throat/pharynx area—more on the left side, starting around my left tonsil. The sharp “knife-stroke” pain is there, not in the chest, head, ears, sinuses, or abdomen.
Yes—swallowing is hard, and I’m making more saliva than usual. I also have trouble breathing, with noisy breathing (stridor) and hoarseness, like my airway is tight.
I do have a hoarse voice, and my throat feels very painful. I don’t know about fully opening my mouth, and I don’t have drooling that I can see—just the extra saliva.
